name: THE PUSHER
blurb: The blue one is who you are unless a board says otherwise. Walk into a crate to push it, and never pull, so where you stand decides which way a crate can go.
practice: Push the crate onto the marker, then try to get it back off. You cannot.

name: THE SWAPPER
blurb: The violet one touches nothing. Moving trades places with the first crate down that line however far off it is, which is the only way anything here moves a crate towards itself.
practice: Trade with the crate across the room. Nothing in between is touched.

name: THE WADER
blurb: Water carries this one. What stops everything else on the board is a road, and a crate pushed in is still lost.
practice: Walk out across the water, which nothing else in this gallery can do.

name: A PARTY
blurb: A board can have more than one of you on it. Only one takes the controls at a time, and pointing them at somebody else costs a move like anything else.
practice: The marker in the corner can only be shoved into, and the crate in the other corner can only be dragged out. Take each of them in turn.

name: THE PHASER
blurb: A single wall is one step rather than a stop, so long as there is floor to arrive on. Two walls thick is still a wall.
practice: Step through the thin wall. Then try the thick one.

name: THE WARDEN
blurb: Light does not harm this one. A beam that ends every other run is scenery, and the squares behind it are simply squares.
practice: Walk straight through the beam.

name: ICE
blurb: Anything that steps onto ice keeps going the way it was going until something stops it.
practice: Push the crate east along the ice, then walk onto the ice yourself.

name: PITS
blurb: A crate pushed into a pit fills it and is spent. The filled pit is floor from then on, so a bridge costs a crate.
practice: One crate fills the hole and the other crosses it. There is no way round.

name: PLATES AND GATES
blurb: A gate is open while a plate of its group is held down, by a crate or by you. Standing on it yourself opens it, but then you are standing on it.
practice: Step on the plate and watch the gate. Then park one crate on it and walk the other through.

name: PORTALS
blurb: Matching pads swap places. Crates travel too, which is how a crate reaches somewhere you could never push it.
practice: Step onto the pad. There is no other way to the far side of the wall.

name: ELEVATORS
blurb: Shafts join storeys. Stand on one and a prompt appears over your head: Q rides up, E rides down.
practice: Ride up, look around the upper storey, and ride back down.

name: CRATES IN SHAFTS
blurb: A crate pushed into a shaft rides it, down when there is a storey below and up when there is not.
practice: Push the crate into the shaft, then take the other shaft down to meet it.

name: ONE WAY
blurb: An arrow square takes traffic one way only. It costs nothing to go with it and there is no going back against it.
practice: Push the crate along the arrows, then try to walk back through one.

name: BELTS
blurb: A belt carries whatever lands on it its own way, not the way that thing was going, so it can turn a crate off the line you pushed it down.
practice: Push the crate onto the belt and watch it turn, then step on yourself.

name: FRAGILE FLOOR
blurb: Pale floor holds once. Step off it, or slide over it, and it drops away behind you, so a route through it is a route you only have while you are on it.
practice: Walk east over the two pale squares, then try to walk back.

name: SWITCHES
blurb: A switch throws its gate and leaves it thrown. A plate has to be held down by something; a switch remembers, so you can walk away and take the crate with you.
practice: Throw the switch, walk back, and take the crate through the gate it opened.

name: BRITTLE WALLS
blurb: A cracked wall gives way to a crate, which is spent breaking it. That is a second use for a spare, and the only way through some walls.
practice: Spend the near crate on the wall, then walk round for the other one.

name: WATER
blurb: Water takes a crate and keeps it. Unlike a pit it is no shallower afterwards, so a crate spent here buys nothing at all.
practice: Lose the first crate in the water, then walk the long way round with the other.

name: THE DRAGGER
blurb: The green one drags and cannot shove at all. Hold SHIFT and step away from a crate and it comes with you, so it reaches the corners a shover never can and loses the shove entirely.
practice: Hold SHIFT and step away from the crate to drag it out. Walking into it does nothing.

name: THE MAGNET
blurb: The red one drags whatever it steps away from, asked or not, and cannot shove either. Every move is a decision about what is behind as well as what is ahead.
practice: Walk about and watch the crate follow. Getting free of one takes planning.

name: THE BLINKER
blurb: The yellow one treats a gap as a road. Walk into open air and it carries you over to the first ground on the far side, which is the only way anything gets between two islands. Crates stay where they are: nothing but the blinker crosses.
practice: Walk into the empty air. You land on the next ground along.

name: PAIRS
blurb: Where the rule allows it one shove moves two crates in a line, so a pair that would jam each other travels together instead.
practice: Push both crates the whole way with one line of shoves.

name: BEAMS
blurb: An emitter throws a beam and never stops. Walk into one and it takes you, and the move you died on comes straight back.
practice: The tower is drinking the beam and the door is open while it does. Then step into the beam and watch the board rewind.

name: MIRRORS
blurb: A mirror turns a beam a quarter turn and is otherwise a thing standing on its square. Light that would have run into a wall goes round the corner instead.
practice: Seat the gem and follow what it throws. The mirror is what puts it on the tower, and the tower is what opens the door.

name: ORBS AND TOWERS
blurb: A tower drinks a beam and powers its gate for as long as one reaches it. An orb is a crate that stops light, so parking one in the way puts the gate back down.
practice: An orb shoves like a crate and stops light like one. Take it through the door the tower is holding.

name: LAMPS
blurb: A lamp is shoved about like anything else and throws light a few squares in every direction. A sensor holds its gate for as long as a lamp is reaching it.
practice: Push the lamp one square nearer and watch the sensor open its eye.

name: SHADOWS
blurb: Light stops at what stops it. A crate between the lamp and the sensor puts the sensor in shadow, and where the shadow falls is worked out rather than looked at.
practice: Push the crate into the column of light and watch the sensor go dark.

name: MOMENTUM
blurb: Speed survives a portal. Come out of a pad with ice straight ahead and the slide picks up again, which throws a crate somewhere no push could reach.
practice: Push the crate into the pad with one move, then step in after it and ride.

name: GEMS AND SOCKETS
blurb: A gem is carried rather than shoved. Stand on one and press SPACE to lift it, carry it to a socket, and press SPACE again to seat it. A seated gem throws light of its own colour the way the plinth is pointing.
practice: Lift the gem, shove the crate out of the gap, and seat the gem in the plinth.

name: LIGHT THAT LENDS
blurb: Standing in coloured light lends you what the colour is for, for exactly as long as you stand in it. Ruby is a wall you may step through.
practice: Seat the gem, stand in what it throws, and walk into the wall. Step out of the light first and the wall is a wall.

name: AMBER AND BOULDERS
blurb: A boulder is the one thing on the board that no shove moves. Amber light lends the hands for it, so a boulder is a wall until you are standing in the right colour.
practice: Seat the gem and walk into the boulder from inside the amber light. Then try it from outside.

name: THE BREAKER
blurb: The Breaker shoves like anybody and breaks a boulder bare handed, so the one obstacle nothing else answers is the one this class walks through.
practice: Walk into the boulder. Then push the crate onto the marker.

name: GLASS
blurb: A pane stops a body and lets light straight through, which is the one wall on the board a beam does not care about.
practice: The wall stops you and the pane in it does not stop the beam, so the tower on the far side is lit and the door is open.

name: LENSES
blurb: A lens stains whatever light crosses it. A beam that kills goes in and a beam that lends comes out, so a board with a lens on it can make a colour it owns no gem of.
practice: Walk into the green light and keep going. Jade is water you may walk on, for as long as the light reaches you.

name: SPLITTERS
blurb: A wedge cuts a beam in two and throws the halves out either side of the line it came in on, so one stone lights two towers and opens two doors at once.
practice: Seat the gem. Both towers take a half of the beam, and the crate's road has a door held by each.

name: SPIKES
blurb: A bed of spikes is a door that only bars bodies. It stands up while its group is powered and lies flat when it is not, and a crate crosses it either way.
practice: The spikes are up while the plate is held. Take the crate off it, cross, and deliver the other one.

name: THE BURNER
blurb: A burner is a fire under two steel leaves. They hold under you and give under a crate, so what is pushed onto one is gone for good. Unlike a hole it never fills, and unlike water it is ground to walk on.
practice: Every crate has to end on a marker and there is only one marker, so one of them goes in the fire.

name: WATCHERS
blurb: A watcher kills whatever is beside it, which is the four squares around it and not the corners. It never moves on its own, and the only way to move one is to trade places with it from far enough off to still be alive when you arrive.
practice: Trade with the watcher across the corridor, then take the crate to the marker.

name: SHUTTERS
blurb: A shutter is a gate read backwards: shut while its group is powered and open while it is not. One plate can hold a door open and a shutter closed at the same time, so opening the way on is closing the way back.
practice: Go in by the shutter while it is open. Putting the crate on the plate opens the gate and shuts the shutter behind you.

name: LOCKS
blurb: A lock answers to what is in your hands rather than to anything on the board. It stands open for as long as somebody is carrying a gem of its colour, and shuts again the moment the gem is put down.
practice: Lift the gem and take the crate through the lock. Then put the gem down and try again.

name: MIRRORS ON PALLETS
blurb: A mirror on a pallet turns a beam the way one set into the floor does and shoves the way a crate does, so where the light ends up is something you push around the room.
practice: Shove the pallet along the beam until the light turns onto the tower. Push it from the dark side: the mirror is what is keeping you out of the beam.
